title: CommandsOutput
description: The command tree `duckduckgo-search-cli commands` writes on stdout, discriminated by `type: "commands"`. This is the surface an agent reads to discover the argv it may build, so an undeclared shape here costs more than an undeclared search field: a wrong assumption becomes a wrong invocation. Added in v1.0.3 (GAP-SCHEMA-INTROSPECTION-UNDECLARED-001) — the subcommand had shipped with no published contract at all. English-only: these keys are clap metadata, not search-result fields, and the payload is serialized directly, bypassing the wire-key mapper.

version.description: Crate version that produced this tree. The tree is compiled in, so it is exact for this binary and says nothing about any other.

root.description: The root command. Its own `name` is the binary name; every invocable subcommand hangs beneath it.

agent_ops.description: Which agent-native reductions each surface can honour (v1.0.4+). Published so a caller learns the contract instead of discovering it by collecting exit codes. Until v1.0.4 these flags were accepted by every surface and silently ignored by most of them; now each one either applies or is refused with exit 2, and this table says in advance which.

error_contract.description: Where each class of failure is written and in what shape (v1.0.5+). The three classes were individually consistent and collectively undiscoverable: a caller told to parse stdout for `type == "error"` sees the validation class, misses the usage class because it is written to stderr, and mis-handles the runtime class because its `error` is a string where the others carry an object. Publishing the split changes no behaviour; it removes the need to learn it by collecting exit codes.

flag_position.description: Where the eight agent-native flags are accepted on the command line. They belong to the root argument group, so placing one after the subcommand is a clap usage error, not a capability refusal — a distinction that is invisible from the exit code alone, since both are 2.

error_channel.title: one failure class and the channel it is written to

class.description: Stable identifier for the failure class.

stream.description: Which stream carries the envelope. Measured against the binary by `error_contract_matches_the_binary`, never merely asserted here.

schema.description: Published schema id this envelope conforms to. Resolve it with `duckduckgo-search-cli schema --name <id>`.

discriminator.description: How a parser tells this envelope apart from a success payload and from the other failure classes.

raised_by.description: What produces this class, with a concrete example.

flag_position.title: where the agent-native flags are accepted

otherwise.description: What happens in any other position, and why it is not a capability refusal.

surface.description: Surface name as the operator types it, e.g. `doctor` or `config list`.

discriminator_key.description: The KEY an agent reads to route this envelope, or null when it has none. Renamed from `discriminator` in v1.0.5: the field was documented as the key and the table behind it held the VALUE (`doctor`, `schema_catalog`, `config_list`) while every emitted envelope carries the key `type`. An agent that trusted the published matrix went looking for a key named `doctor` and found nothing. The slot always meant the key — that is what the reduction code compares against — so the data was corrected and the name now says which of the two it is.

identity.description: Keys whose values `--truncate-content` will NOT shorten on this surface, because they are contract IDENTIFIERS rather than prose: a string the agent hands back to a program. Config keys go back into `config set`, locale tags into `--ui-lang`, schema ids into `schema --name`. Added in v1.0.5, after `schema --truncate-content 12` was measured turning `invoke` into `duckduckgo-s` and `id` into `searc` — a command line that no longer runs and a name the CLI rejects.

rows.description: Key holding the row array the row operations act on. Null means the envelope has no rows, so `--filter`, `--sort`, `--dedupe-by`, `--limit` and `--count-only` are refused with exit 2 rather than ignored. Declared per surface, never inferred: `doctor` carries both `checks` and `failed_checks`, and guessing between them would answer a question the operator did not ask.

supports.description: Flags that do something on this surface. Anything absent is refused, never silently dropped.

about.description: Short help text. Null when the command declares none — absent help is not an error.

hidden.description: True for commands kept out of `--help`, such as the legacy `buscar` alias. They remain invocable, so an agent may still call them; they are simply not advertised.

subcommands.description: Children, recursively. An empty array is a leaf, not a missing field.
